After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding the rollout of its new iPad interface, which includes a refreshed Mac-style sidebar. Here's what you need to know.

WhatsApp is developing a brand new iPad app interface

Although WhatsApp began adapting its iOS app to the major Liquid Glass visual overhaul as early as October last year, the company only brought the new design to the iPad for small-scale testing in June this year.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the new design included Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons, and context menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on the iPhone.

According to the website's latest report, WhatsApp is now rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the default bottom tab bar layout with a Mac-style sidebar.

This sidebar follows the layout already used in WhatsApp's Mac version, allowing users to quickly access chats, status updates, communities, calls, Meta AI, and other parts of the app. Users can also hide the sidebar to free up more space for the chat list and conversation view.

Here is the report:

WABetaInfo points out that the new sidebar is now available to some testers using the latest TestFlight version, but some users on the regular App Store version have also begun seeing this feature.

As is typical of WhatsApp's rollout approach, regardless of whether users are on the Beta or official version, the new interface may take some time to reach all users. However, iPad users will ultimately benefit from a more tablet-appropriate layout.
